newsitem.title: UK: Shell Oil profit at top end of London forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Shell Oil profit at top end of London forecasts.

text.p: First quarter results of Shell Oil came in at the top end of the range of London analysts' forecasts.
But the deviance between forecasts and actual results was not big enough to warrant a revision of profit estimates for the parent Royal Dutch/Shell Group, some industry watchers said.
Shell Oil earlier reported adjusted first quarter net income rose to $499 million from $385 million ahead of the release of the Shell Group results on May 1.
"The bottom line figure was about $20 million higher (than I expected), which is essentially nothing at all," said Nick Antill at BZW. "There won't be any changes to our forecasts," he added.
Analysts here had expected earnings of Shell Oil, the U.S. unit of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, to roughly fall between 450 and 500 million stg.
"It (the results) come in at the top end of expectations and that is very encouraging," said Paul Spedding of Kleinwort Benson.
He was waiting for more details on Shell Oil's results before deciding whether to change his forecast for Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
